narrative:
The model determined that you have a 59% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, your credit history, and the existence of other installment plans. Your checking account status of 0-200 DM was the single biggest reason for the denial. Most approved applicants (59%) have no checking account at all or maintain higher balances, so this limited positive balance pushed the prediction noticeably toward higher risk.

Your credit history of having critical or other existing credits actually worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward approval. This was the second most important factor and helped offset some of the risk signaled by your account status.

The third strongest influence was that you have an active installment plan with a bank. This detail increased the perceived risk because the majority of approved applicants (87%) have no other installment commitments.

Taken together, these factors led the model to conclude that the risk was too high to approve the loan. To improve your chances next time, focus on building a stronger checking account balance and reducing or completing your existing installment obligations before reapplying. This would directly address the two issues that hurt your application most. (218 words)
